I'd like to rest under a roof tonight.

숲에서 약초와 쓸 만한 것을 찾는 여행자: A traveler who forages herbs and useful things in the forest
창문 불빛이 보여서\n얼마나 반가웠는지 몰라요.\n오늘 밤, 잘 부탁합니:

I'm in your care tonight.
숲에서는 이름을 불러도\n돌아보지 말라던데…\n여기서는 쉬어도 되겠죠?:

I'm in your debt again.

교역 마차를 호위해 온 용병: A mercenary who guarded a trade wagon
마녀든 누구든 상관없소.\n불이 켜진 집이면 됐지.\n따뜻한 수프도 있겠:
Witch or not, I don't care.
A house with a lit fire will do.
There's warm soup, I hope?
There were footprints on the path.

그 수프가 생각나서 왔소.\n방 하나 비어 있겠지?:
I came back for that soup.
You've got a room free, right?
오래된 산길을 아는 호위꾼: A guard who knows the old mountain paths

I'll sleep well tonight.

There's no chapel around here.
The same room again, please.
Preferably far from the window.
눈 덮인 고개를 넘는 편지 배달부: A letter carrier crossing snowy passes
여기가 그 마녀의 산장이에요?\n생각보다 아늑하네요!\n하룻밤 잘 부탁해:
Is this the witch's lodge?
It's cozier than I expected!
I'll be staying one night.
숲에서 누가 제 이름을 불렀어요.\n편지 받을 사람은 아니었는데…:
Someone in the forest called my name.
They weren't anyone I deliver to...
I didn't get lost today!
I followed your chimney smoke.
숲의 옛 문양을 찾아다니는 학자: A scholar who hunts the forest's old sigils
A bed offered by a witch...
More stories to record.
I saw the same sigil in the ruins.
But it looked different coming and going.
I brought plenty of ink this time.
The forest keeps adding to the tale.
마을과 산길 사이를 오가는 상인: A merchant between the village and mountain paths
소문보다 창문 불빛을 믿어요.\n방 하나 부탁할게요.\n값은 제대로 치를:
I trust a lit window over rumors.
One room, please.
I'll pay a fair price.
Strange, isn't it? Every time I leave
the forest, I carry one more thing.
The fire's lit again today.
Nothing's better after a day of trading.
광산 경비로 늙은 퇴역 드워프: A retired dwarf who grew old as a mine guard
Let me knock on the wall first.
...Hm, solid through.
Built well for a witch's house.
Things outside can't cross walls.
They cross doors.
Give me a spot by the door.
Back again. The roof beams

That's worth my lodging fee.
석궁 한 자루로 산을 넘는 드워프: A dwarf who crosses mountains with one crossbow
내기 하나 하지, 마녀!\n오늘 밤 내가 먼저 자나\n숲이 먼저 조용해지:

Will I fall asleep first tonight,
or the forest go quiet first?
동전 하나 걸고 말하지.\n저 숲엔 다리 여덟 달린 게 있어.\n…맞혔지:
One coin says there's something
eight-legged in that forest.
...Right, wasn't I? Now buy me a drink.
또 왔다! 저번 내기는\n내가 졌으니 숙박비는 두 배.\n드워프는 빚을:
I'm back! I lost the last bet,
so double the lodging fee.
Dwarves leave no debts.
The door... is oak.
Cut against the grain.
Still serviceable.
이 숲 나무는 결이 꼬였소.\n뭔가에 눌리며 자란 거지.\n베기 전에 먼:
The trees here have twisted grain.
They grew under some weight.
Listen to them before you fell them.
저번에 본 들보 말이오.\n쐐기 하나면 백 년은 가.\n내일 아침에 박아:
That beam I saw last time:
one wedge keeps it a hundred years.
I'll drive it in tomorrow morning.
이끼와 광석을 함께 캐는 드워프 노파: An old dwarf woman who gathers moss and ore together
The tea's gone cold.
...No, I'll warm it.
You just lock the door properly.
창턱 이끼는 왜 안 긁어?\n약으로 쓰면 좋은 건데.\n쯧, 내가 긁어:
Why don't you scrape the sill moss?
It makes good medicine.
Tsk, I'll do it myself.
That face again.
You haven't slept all night, have you?
Eat your soup and sit.
돌에 새긴 것만 믿는 드워프: A dwarf who trusts only what's carved in stone
이 산장 주춧돌…\n사람 손으로 깎은 게 아니군.\n하룻밤 묵으며 살펴보:
This Lodge's foundation stone...
Not cut by human hands.
I'll stay a night and study it.
종이에 적은 건 믿지 않소.\n돌에 새긴 것만 남지.\n지하에 뭐가 있소:
I don't trust what's written on paper.
Only what's carved in stone remains.
What's underground here?
I'm back. That stone is
warmer than last time.
Stone doesn't lie.
모루를 등에 지고 다니는 드워프: A dwarf who carries his anvil on his back
...Room.
The hinges squeak.
I'll fix them in the morning.
I changed the door handle.
No charge.
I slept well.
...Back again.
Your axe blade was dull.
I sharpened it.
술통을 메고 산을 넘는 드워프: A dwarf who carries a keg over the mountains
마녀의 산장!\n술 얘기는 많이 들었어요.\n…아, 없다고요? 제가 있죠:
The Witch's Lodge!
I've heard plenty about the drink.
...Oh, there's none? I'm here, aren't I!
숲에서 노래를 들었는데\n제 노래보다 음이 낮더라고요.\n한 잔 하고 잊:
I heard singing in the forest,
lower-pitched than mine.
I'll have a drink and forget it.
지난번 통은 비었어요?\n이번 건 더 진해요.\n굴뚝 연기 보고 달려왔죠:
Is last time's keg empty?
This one's stronger.
I ran here at the sight of your smoke.
엉겅퀴 창을 든 작은 수호자: A small guardian with a thistle spear
작은 몸의 큰 격식: Great formality in a small body
숲의 수호자 티슬,\n산장의 주인께 예를 갖춥니다.\n창은 문 옆에 세워:
Thistle, guardian of the forest,

I'll stand my spear by the door.
Darkness is spreading its roots.
My spear is small,
but it has never backed down.
We meet again.
I chased off last night's
crow from your roof.
나뭇가지 활을 쏘는 장난꾸러기 요정: A mischievous fairy who shoots a twig bow

three cobwebs, one spider.
숲의 눈들이 늘었어요.\n하나는 제가 맞혔고요.\n…농담이에요. 둘이에요:
The forest's eyes have multiplied.
I hit one of them.
...Just kidding. Two.
I'm back!
This time, a hundred pine-needle arrows.
I'll give you one as a gift.
병든 가지만 자른다는 요정 정원사: A fairy gardener who cuts only diseased branches
베는 게 아니오. 치는 거지.\n병든 가지만.\n그 차이를 아는 집이면:

Only the diseased branches.
If this house knows the difference, I'll stay.
저 숲은 가지치기가 안 됐소.\n썩은 가지에 썩은 것이 깃들지.\n내일:
That forest hasn't been pruned.
Rot nests in rotten branches.
I'll take up my saw tomorrow.
That branch from last time
healed well.
...The praise is for the tree.
씨앗 주머니를 품에 안은 요정: A fairy hugging a pouch of seeds

...So am I.
창가에서 씨앗 하나가\n자꾸 숲 쪽으로 굴러가요.\n…따라가면 안 되겠죠:
One seed by the window keeps
rolling toward the forest.
...I shouldn't follow it, should I?
또 왔어요.\n지난번 씨앗이 싹을 냈어요.\n…보여 드려도 돼요?:
I'm back.
Last time's seed has sprouted.
...May I show you?
오염된 숲의 소식을 전하는 요정: A fairy bearing news of the corrupted forest
숲의 이름으로 묻습니다.\n이 집의 불은\n무엇을 태워 밝힙니까?:
In the forest's name, I ask:
What does this house
burn to light its fire?
북쪽 샘이 검게 변했습니다.\n숲은 당신을 지켜보고 있습니다.\n…좋은:

your name ill.
도토리 배낭을 멘 숨 가쁜 요정: A breathless fairy with an acorn pack
하아, 하아, 도착!\n씨앗 열둘 배달 중이에요.\n하나도 안 잃었어요!:

잠결에 숲의 꿈을 받아 적는 요정: A fairy who writes down the forest's dreams in her sleep

고물 갑옷을 짜 맞춘 고블린 용사: A goblin hero in armor pieced together from scrap

Just one room. The innermost one.
The forest's eyes? Saw 'em!
Not scared one bit!
...Okay, two was a bit scary.

Back again. I counted.

...You don't believe me. Count them.
톱을 세 자루 지고 다니는 고블린: A goblin who carries three saws

Heh heh, nice house.

숲 나무는 톱날이 무뎌져.\n뭔가가 안에서 버티거든.\n그래도 셋째 톱이:

...I'll just look. A room, please.
숲에서 반짝이는 걸 주웠어요.\n…눈이었어요. 누구 눈인진 몰라요.\n주:

또 왔어요! 주머니 하나 늘었어요.\n뭘 넣을진 아직 몰라요.\n여기서:
I'm back! One more pocket.

I'll find something here!
흥정으로 인사를 대신하는 고블린: A goblin who haggles instead of saying hello
흥정으로 시작하는 인사: A greeting that starts with haggling
숙박비요? 반값은 어때요?\n…안 돼요? 그럼 제값에\n이 단추 하나 얹:
Lodging fee? How about half?
...No? Then full price,
and I'll throw in this button.
숲에서 물건을 잃었어요.\n근데 손해 본 느낌이 아니에요.\n거래를 한:
I lost something in the forest.

찢어진 지도를 펼치는 고블린: A goblin unfurling a torn map

...Well, just me, but about ten times.
또 왔소! 지도가 늘었어!\n여기, 이 집이 그려져 있지.\n…내가 그렸:
I'm back! More maps!
See, this house is drawn here.
...I drew it. Yesterday.
외알 안경으로 값을 매기는 고블린: A goblin who appraises through a monocle
흠. 문고리는 평범.\n등불은… 오래됐군요.\n방값보다 비싸요. 묵을게요:
Hm. Door handle: ordinary.
The lantern... is old.
Worth more than the room. I'll stay.
숲에서 동전을 주웠어요.\n한 번도 본 적 없는 얼굴이\n새겨져 있더군요:
I found a coin in the forest.
It bears a face I've never seen.
I can't put a price on it.
또 왔어요.\n지난번 그 등불, 아직 있죠?\n팔진 마세요. 제가 살 거:
I'm back.
That lantern from last time, still here?
Don't sell it. I'm buying it.
찢긴 귀의 늑대 수인 검사: A wolf beastfolk swordsman with a torn ear

I sleep lightly.
That's the pack's habit.
The forest's scent has changed.
Iron and rotting leaves.
...I'll stay awake tonight.
...Back again.
This house smells of a pack.
Not bad.
밤눈이 밝은 삵 수인 궁수: A leopard-cat beastfolk archer with keen night sight
I see better at night.
A window seat will do.
Twelve eyes in the forest.
Eight are beasts. Four aren't.
Back again.
Your chimney smoke is the first thing I see.
꿀단지를 찬 곰 수인 벌목꾼: A bear beastfolk lumberjack with a honey pot at his belt
으음… 따뜻하군.\n겨울잠 자기 좋은 집이야.\n…아, 자러 온 건 아니:
Mmm... warm.
A fine house to hibernate in.
...Ah, not that I came to sleep.
숲의 것들이 시끄럽더군.\n곰은 겨울에 시끄러운 걸\n안 좋아해. 조용히:
The forest things are loud.
Bears don't like noise in winter.
I'll have to quiet them.
Back again. Want some honey?
...Half. Winter's long.
귀를 접고 두리번대는 토끼 수인: A rabbit beastfolk with folded ears, glancing around
E-excuse me!
The room can be small.
Something like a burrow is even better.
숲에서 뭔가가 따라왔어요.\n돌아보진 않았어요.\n대신 약초를 세 배 캤:
Something followed me in the forest.
I didn't look back.
But I picked triple the herbs!
또 왔어요! 안 늦었죠?\n바구니 가득이에요.\n…뒤에 아무도 없죠?:
I'm back! Not late, am I?
The basket's full.
...There's no one behind me, right?
숲길을 꿰고 있다는 여우 수인: A fox beastfolk who claims to know every forest path
길을 잃은 건 아니에요.\n길이 저를 잃은 거죠.\n덕분에 좋은 집을 찾:
I'm not lost.
The path lost me.
And so I found a lovely house.
The forest paths keep changing.
I memorize them by tail, so I'm fine,
but others, well...
Your regular is here!
Took a shortcut this time.
...It took half a day longer, though.
짐을 절대 내려놓지 않는 오소리 수인: A badger beastfolk who never sets down his load
I don't put the pack down.
Not even to sleep.
Just give me a roomy room.
Something tugged my pack in the forest.
I held on.
...Didn't look at what it was.
Back again.
The pack got bigger.
Don't ask.
밤에만 날아다니는 올빼미 수인: An owl beastfolk who flies only at night
밤에 깨어나는 전령: A courier who wakes at night
낮에 문을 두드려 미안해요.\n해 지면 깨어날게요.\n그때 소식을 전하죠:
Sorry for knocking by day.
I'll wake when the sun sets.
Then I'll deliver my news.
I heard it in the night forest.
A voice calling to a stone.
...The one beneath your house.
The night guest is back.
Your window light
can be seen from the sky.
맹세를 뼈에 새긴 오크 호위대장: An orc guard captain with oaths carved into her bones
To one who offers a roof,
I owe my sword.
That is our law.
The forest things eye the door.
While I stand before it,
it will not open.
I have returned.
Last time's debt remains.
I will repay it tonight.
사냥감을 자랑하는 오크 투창수: An orc spear-thrower who brags about her catch
토끼 셋, 꿩 둘!\n오늘 저녁은 내가 낸다.\n솥은 있겠지?:
Three rabbits, two pheasants!
Dinner's on me tonight.
You have a pot, right?
The forest beasts are fewer.
Something's hunting ahead of me.
...My prey.
I'm back! A deer this time!
...Left half in the forest.
Something took it.
나무에게 사과하고 베는 오크 거구: A hulking orc who apologizes to trees before felling them
나무에게 사과하는 거구: A giant who apologizes to trees
Ha ha! The door's small!
...Did I break it? No? Good.
I'll go in carefully.
